item.title: How To Learn
item.description: My buddy Arthur recently shared this with me, his synthesis of research he’s been doing on how to be a more effective learner. Stay engaged Choose to find the information useful Be invested in tackling difficult problems Try to anticipate what’s next Identify big idea Use them as anchor to connect details Periodically summarize what you’ve heard Keep conclusions tentative Evaluate evidence, don’t accept it at face value Ask followup questions Don’t get derailed Concentrate on the message, not the messenger Don’t get thrown off by emotionally charged language Don’t stop listening when you disagree Humanize the presenter, get to know them Adjust note taking to the presenter’s patterns Seriously - how great is that?

item.title: Playing with Elixir is just FUN
item.description:
I’ve been using Elixir for a few weeks now, sometimes forcing it to play nice with Mongodb/Meteor , which it doesn’t really want to do. Sometimes with Posgres (which it loves). Sometimes just plain ole’ Elixir with no persistance.

It is realllllly fun!

item.title: Meteor and Elixir (part one) A Rocky Courtship
item.description:
I have been watching Elixir for almost 2 years now, and debating if it’s mature enough for me to invest in.

Obviously Erlang is super-mature, and Elixir is quite stable, but it’s a question of “is the community mature enough yet?”

Since I’m now writing this, I believe it is “ready”, and I’m beginning a journey to build out some services in Elixir to stand up next to existing node services (meteorjs) and slow move funcitonality over to to Elixir.

Chapter One: Proof of Concept, Mongo is supposed to be Simple.

item.title: Meteor 1.5 ~ Bundle Optimization + Examples
item.description:
I have been playing with Meteor 1.5 and it’s dynamic imports, which can be used to reduce the amount of javascript code sent to the browser.

This article is a deep dive into how to profile and optimize your client side code to make smarter use of the new dynamic imports…

Which will make meteor load faster for your users.

item.title: 2017 Memorial Day Homework
item.description: 2017 Memorial Day Homework I have made the formal household declaration that all screen time will be matched, hour-for-hour with project time. Yesterday we cleaned the 1st floor, mopped and everything. Today we went grocery shopping, made lunch, and then started on homework time. To say that I am unpopular here, would be an understatement. But both of our kids will benefit from some extra assignments. Our education system is super lax, and a bit of supplemental assignment seems like a good idea.

item.title: CoreOS and Docker great presentation

item.title: Life Changingly Good TED Radio Hour
Meteor 092rc1 with Cordova
item.description: Meteor 0.9.2-rc1 is fun to play with, Cordova support functional Last night I started playing with meteor –release 0.9.2-rc1. It’s wonderful! The local development and hot-code-push is a great improvement. Builds were painless (mostly). The hot code push works brilliantly in the simulator. This is going to be a game changer for mobile development with Meteor.

item.title: About
item.description: About Alan Blount I’m an AI/ML Engineer at Google in Boulder, Colorado, working on cutting-edge generative AI systems and agent memory architectures. I’ve been at Google for several years, focusing on building the infrastructure and tools that power the next generation of intelligent systems. Current Work at Google At Google, I’m deeply involved in: Generative AI Systems: Building and deploying large-scale AI applications Agent Memory Architectures: Designing memory systems that help AI agents remember and learn Memory Bank Platforms: Contributing to Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Memory Bank deployment Production AI Infrastructure: Scaling AI systems to handle millions of users Open Source & Community I believe in giving back to the developer community through open source contributions:
